reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the formation of isolated Pt/Pd sites, charge transfer, enhanced adsorption, and superior catalytic performance in PtPdCoCuNi HEA, but it does not address the role of low-temperature synthesis in restricting precursor mobility or driving stochastic mixing—those mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Low-temperature synthesis inhibits precursor mobility and drives stochastic mixing, preventing segregation.
Stochastic mixing yields isolated Pt and Pd sites uniformly dispersed in a single-phase HEA matrix.
Isolated Pt/Pd sites undergo charge transfer from surrounding base metals, modulating their electronic structure.
Electronic modulation enhances reactant adsorption and catalytic activity compared to aggregated or bimetallic systems.
The PtPdCoCuNi HEA catalyst shows higher nitrobenzene hydrogenation yield than PtPd controls.
